_comment: Pinned Microsoft SDK versions. Single source of truth for which SDK builds this
library is tested against. Bump deliberately, never automatically: Microsoft requires
apps to stay on recent SDK versions and has previously blocked launches for apps that
fell behind, so a bump is a release-worthy change.
iOS 21.x requires iOS 17+ and Xcode 26. If a consumer must support iOS 16, they need
SDK 20.x, which Microsoft supports for high-priority security fixes only. See SPEC.md.

_notes: IntuneMAMStatic.xcframework is the static variant — not used; the dynamic one keeps
bundle size down when extensions are involved.
libIntuneMAMSwiftFileProvider.xcframework is only for File Provider extensions.
IntuneMAMResources.bundle carries every SDK screen (PIN, blur, diagnostics, MTD
compliance) and 28 localizations. Without it the SDK's UI cannot render.

_comment: A version bump forces a conscious check against the MAM compatibility matrix and the
msal_android has no requirement from Microsoft to satisfy. The Android SDK guide says
only "integrate MSAL" and links the MSAL repository, unlike iOS where the coupling is
hard. So this is our choice, pinned for reproducibility rather than compatibility:
msal_ios is exact, not a range: the Intune SDK does not carry its own MSAL, it drives
the app's. Two consumers on different MSALs is the same hazard pinning the Intune SDK
exists to prevent. Resolved by CocoaPods on 2026-09-04, not guessed.
`requires` is the compatibility-matrix row for the pinned Android tag above (12.4.0 ->
the 12.0.0 row). Microsoft tests these combinations; mixing rows is untested. These are
the library's own defaults in android/build.gradle. The consumer's app module, where the
MAM Gradle plugin actually runs, must land on the same row -- that is O-E, still open.
